significance: A shrine cut into a huge rock at Methala near Perumbavoor, originally Jain and turned into a Bhagavathi temple in the ninth century, with rock-carved images of the Tirthankaras Parshvanatha and Mahavira alongside Padmavati. Reached by sixty-nine steps and roofed by a single vast boulder, it is a protected monument of the Kerala State Department of Archaeology.
story: A woman of great beauty is said to have been seen playing with stones in the forest and to have vanished into the cave with them, the stone she tossed up becoming the roof of the shrine.
